name: Cheekbone smashing

card.summary: A claimed bonesmashing practice of striking the cheekbones in the belief they will heal thicker and more prominent, giving a more sculpted midface.
card.note: Surgeons report striking the face can cause fractures, nerve and vessel injury and deformity.

quick.overview:
Cheekbone smashing is a variant of bonesmashing in which people say they hit the cheekbones, in the belief that bone remodels as it heals and becomes more projected. The stated goal is a chiselled, higher-cheekbone look.

It is often described by commentators as an inside joke that is rarely carried out. Facial surgeons warn that blows to the face can fracture the zygomatic bones, misalign the face and injure nerves, vessels and the eyes. No research supports it as a way to change cheekbone shape.
quick.how: Within the community it is discussed as an idea rather than a routine; no instructions are given here. Those seeking more prominent cheekbones typically turn to documented routes such as weight and body-fat changes, makeup contouring, fillers or implants performed by clinicians.
quick.risks: Facial trauma can cause fractures, misalignment, nerve and blood vessel injury, deformity and vision changes, according to facial surgeons summarised in reference sources. The zygomatic bone forms part of the eye socket, which is why injuries near it can affect the eye.

lead: Cheekbone smashing is a form of bonesmashing, a looksmaxxing practice in which people claim that striking facial bone with an object leads it to heal thicker and sharper. The cheekbones (zygomatic bones) are one of the target areas named, with the stated aim of a more prominent, angular midface [1].

Wikipedia describes bonesmashing as considered an inside joke that is rarely done, with coverage treating it as a TikTok beauty trend. Doctors have criticised it as misinformation, and facial surgeons warn of fractures, misalignment, nerve and vessel injuries, deformity and vision changes [1].

The zygomatic bone forms the lateral wall and floor of the eye socket and part of the zygomatic arch [2], so blows to the area involve structures around the eye. Those pursuing cheekbone prominence by recognised means use cosmetic procedures such as cheek augmentation, which Wikipedia notes is pursued because high cheekbones are seen as attractive in some cultures [2].

chain: Bone said to remodel while healing
angle.text: Proponents claim healing bone thickens and projects, giving higher cheekbones. Reporting describes it as rare and potentially injurious, and no study shows the effect.

infobox: Fracture, nerve and vessel injury, deformity

paras: The practice is the cheek-specific version of bonesmashing, which proponents say works on the theory that bone adapts to stress and strengthens when it heals [1].
Bonesmashing spread with looksmaxxing on TikTok in the 2020s, according to Wikipedia, which cites news coverage describing it as a beauty trend while noting it is regarded as an inside joke [1].

Facial surgeons quoted in coverage warn of fractures, facial misalignment, nerve and blood vessel injury, facial deformity and vision changes [1]. The cheekbone helps form the orbit, which makes injuries to it significant [2].
No studies found. Clinical literature on zygomatic fractures concerns accidental injury and its repair, not deliberate remodelling.

lore.intro: Cheekbone smashing is mentioned within bonesmashing discussions, often with irony [1].

claims.claim: Hitting the cheekbones makes them heal thicker and more prominent
claims.believers: Proponents point to the idea that bone remodels under stress and heals stronger [1].
claims.experts: Surgeons warn the practice can fracture bone and injure nerves, vessels and eyes; no studies show cosmetic benefit [1].
